title: Make study selectable and let it read firstmate at a pinned SHA
summary: `study` is registered but hidden from the reader, because athena.toml has no [capabilities.study] section. I'll add that section, with its own commands, env and checks, so the reader's catalog and schema offer it. I'll also add a Rust-side way to materialise a source repository read-only at a full pinned SHA, so a study can read firstmate without running it.

defaults_applied.how: The new fetch/pin code gets unit tests on a local fixture repo; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Use the existing athena-git wrapper around git rather than a new git crate.
athena.toml is a governance file, so it is listed and named in a criterion; the pin check is enforced in code, not prose.
A decision entry records the call, with alternatives.
The request is short; I recovered the cause from the wiring, reading.rs and athena.toml.
Only config, a pin-aware source reader, and the tests change. No run step.

assumptions: `study` is already registered in crates/athena-cli/src/wiring.rs; it is hidden only because athena.toml has no [capabilities.study] section, so adding that section is the core of 'selectable'.
The reader's structured-output schema derives its capability enum from the same filtered list, so no change to athena-context is needed beyond tests.
'Read firstmate at a pinned SHA' means reading source files at a commit, not running it; containment and the run step stay deferred per D65.
Agents are hermetic with no network, so fetching must be done by Athena's Rust code (a small git helper in athena-git or athena-cap-study) into a read-only checkout.
firstmate's location is not in the repository; I assume a git URL and SHA are supplied by config or the request.
question: Where does firstmate live (git URL or local path), and which full 40-character SHA should the study pin? I assumed both come from config or the request.

acceptance_criteria.text: athena.toml has a [capabilities.study] section (producer and verifier commands, env, checks) and the change is named as a governance edit; the existing [capabilities.change] section is unchanged.

Run `cargo test --locked`: a new test shows that with the repository's athena.toml the reader's catalog contains both `change` and `study`, and the reader output schema's capability enum is ["change","study",null].

The study capability has a documented, pinned way to read firstmate: a repository URL (or local path) plus a full 40-character commit SHA is recorded in config or the request, and a read of the studied tree is refused unless the SHA is a full id.
Run `cargo test --locked`: tests show that the firstmate source is materialised at exactly the pinned SHA, so a different or missing SHA is an error, using a local fixture repository (no network).

The study producer and verifier grants stay confined: the studied checkout is read-only to agents, the verifier still never writes, and any network fetch happens in Athena's Rust code, not through an agent command.
The study card, the CHANGELOG, and docs/decisions.md (a new D-entry, with alternatives) record the call and say that running firstmate is still out of scope.
Run `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: both are clean.

out_of_scope: Running firstmate or any studied system (containment, run step, replay).
Making any claim about what firstmate contains or does.
Adding study records to AnyRecord or the gate.
Changes to [capabilities.change] or other governance files (workflows, rust-toolchain.toml).
departures: Cost and time are raised above the reference. The request touches governance config, a new fetch-at-SHA mechanism, and tests across several crates, and the fetch design is under-specified.
